STAT5003 Evaluating National Quality Standard Rating Tiers

Group 02

Introduction

Australian education and care services are assessed against the National Quality Standard (NQS) under the National Quality Framework by state and territory regulatory authorities (Australian Children's Education & Care Quality Authority [ACECQA], n.d.-a). ACECQA also publishes national registers containing information about services and providers (ACECQA, n.d.-b). Examining these records may provide useful information for regulatory planning, service improvement and policy research.

Problem Framing & Research Question

This project is a multi-class classification task. Each observation represents an education and care service, and the outcome is its recorded NQS rating tier: Below NQS, Meeting NQS or Above NQS. Model predictions may support further investigation, but they cannot replace formal NQS assessments or establish causal relationships.

The research question is:

To what extent can service type, service capacity, operating patterns, geographic location, and provider characteristics be used to classify an Australian education and care service’s recorded NQS rating tier as Below NQS, Meeting NQS, or Above NQS?

Dataset & Justification

source_dimensions <- read.csv('../outputs/source_dimensions.csv')
linkage_checks <- read.csv('../data/processed/acecqa_linkage_summary.csv')
analysis_data <- read.csv('../data/processed/acecqa_analysis.csv')
stopifnot(linkage_checks$value[linkage_checks$measure == 'Service rows unmatched to provider register'] == 0,
          !anyDuplicated(analysis_data$service_id),
          nrow(analysis_data) == 17160)

This project used two ACECQA national registers downloaded on 18 September 2026: the Education services register and the Approved providers register (ACECQA, n.d.-b). The services register contained 18,183 records and 98 variables, meeting the Large dataset requirement. The providers register contained 10,095 records and 10 variables. Missing ratings, capacity and operating schedules also made the data Messy.

Each observation represented a service. The two registers were linked by Provider Approval Number, meeting the Integrated dataset requirement. IDs were unique in their respective registers, and every service was matched to a provider. After removing 1,023 services without a rating, the final dataset contained 17,160 services from 6,885 providers and 28 candidate predictors. Using the published NQS rating levels (ACECQA, n.d.-a), we grouped ratings into three classes, meeting the Multi-class requirement: Significant Improvement Required and Working Towards NQS became Below NQS; Meeting NQS remained unchanged; and Exceeding NQS and Excellent became Above NQS.

Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

NQS Rating Distribution and Missing Values

The rating tiers were imbalanced: 74.3% of services were Meeting NQS, while 7.4% were Below NQS and 18.3% were Above NQS.

Missingness was high for schedule-specific weekly hours and may be related to which schedules a service offered. Approved capacity was missing for all 307 Family Day Care services. Maximum weekly hours were missing for 142 services; all recorded values were within 168 hours per week.

rating_distribution <- read.csv('../outputs/rating_distribution.csv')
missingness <- read.csv('../outputs/missingness_selected.csv')
knitr::include_graphics(c('../figures/rating_tier_distribution.png',
                          '../figures/missingness_selected.png'))

Rating-tier distribution and missingness in selected variables.

Categorical Variables

Centre-Based Care represented 98.2% of services. Standalone preschool, OSHC services, operating pattern and state showed the clearest relationships with rating tier. Standalone preschools and services without OSHC had a higher proportion of Above NQS ratings, although the groups still overlapped. The three OSHC variables were also strongly related to each other, and service state and provider state often contained similar information.

categorical_counts <- read.csv('../outputs/categorical/categorical_vs_rating_crosstab.csv')
knitr::include_graphics('../figures/categorical_vs_rating_tier.png')

Numerical and Operating Variables

Capacity and approval ages differed across rating tiers, but their distributions overlapped. Provider service count was strongly right-skewed: across service records, the median was 7 and the maximum was 611. Operating hours also differed by rating tier and service type. The Family Day Care group included only 18 Above NQS services, so comparisons within this group were less reliable. Most services (92.4%) recorded five open days per week.

operating_summary <- read.csv('../outputs/operating/operating_by_tier.csv')

Numerical predictors and weekly operating hours by rating tier.

No single predictor clearly separated Below NQS, Meeting NQS and Above NQS services.

Data Preprocessing

Data Preparation and Splitting

Before splitting, approval dates and operating records were used to create age and operating-pattern variables. We also calculated provider service count and whether provider and service states matched. Service and provider IDs, the original rating and other rating-derived variables were excluded from model inputs.

Because a provider may operate several services, we split the data by provider, with approximately 80% for training and 20% for testing. The training set contained 13,497 services from 5,509 providers; the test set contained 3,663 services from 1,376 providers. Each provider’s most common rating tier was used for approximate stratification. Five-fold cross-validation also kept services from the same provider together. Preprocessing values were calculated using each fold’s training data and then applied to its validation data.

Preprocessing Recipes

The shared preprocessing pipelines were implemented with recipes (Kuhn et al., 2026).

Missing values in numerical variables were replaced with the median calculated from the current training data. No separate missingness indicators were created for structural missing values. Missing values in categorical variables were labelled as Unknown. Categories that appeared for the first time in validation or test data were labelled as Novel. Categories representing less than 1% of the training data were grouped as Other.

Logical variables were converted to No/Yes categories, categorical variables were dummy encoded, and predictors with no or very little variation were removed.

kNN and SVM used the shared scaled recipe, which applied a \(\log(x+1)\) transformation to provider_service_count and normalised numerical predictors. LDA used the same recipe and additionally removed linear combinations and numerical predictors with correlations above 0.9. Random Forest used the tree recipe, which also applied the log transformation but did not normalise numerical predictors.

MLR used a separate recipe with 19 selected predictors, normalisation and zero-variance removal. It did not apply the \(\log(x+1)\) transformation to provider_service_count. Detailed code as follows.

# Creates the common outcome, predictor set, train/test split,
# resampling folds, preprocessing specification, and evaluation metrics.SS

  "readr",
  "dplyr",
  "caret",
  "recipes"
)

missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(
    required_packages,
    requireNamespace,
    logical(1),
    quietly = TRUE
  )
]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Install the following packages before running this script: ",

}

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(caret)
library(recipes)


model_data_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/processed/acecqa_analysis.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

required_columns <- c(
  "service_id",
  "provider_id",
  "rating_tier"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(
  required_columns,
  names(model_data_raw)
)

if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Required columns are missing: ",
    paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

model_data_raw <- model_data_raw |>
  mutate(
    rating_tier = factor(
      rating_tier,
      levels = c(
        "Below NQS",
        "Meeting NQS",
        "Above NQS"
      )
    )
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(model_data_raw) > 0,
  !anyDuplicated(model_data_raw$service_id),
  !anyNA(model_data_raw$provider_id),
  !anyNA(model_data_raw$rating_tier)
)

# 80/20 train-test split

split_seed <- 5003L
training_fraction <- 0.80

# A provider may operate services in different rating tiers.
# Use its most frequent tier only as an approximate stratification label.
provider_split_frame <- model_data_raw |>
  count(provider_id, rating_tier, name = "n_services") |>
  group_by(provider_id) |>
  arrange(desc(n_services), rating_tier, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice(1L) |>
  ungroup() |>
  rename(provider_stratum = rating_tier)

set.seed(split_seed)

training_provider_rows <- createDataPartition(
  provider_split_frame$provider_stratum,
  p = training_fraction,
  list = FALSE
)

training_provider_ids <- provider_split_frame$provider_id[
  as.vector(training_provider_rows)
]

training_data <- model_data_raw |>
  filter(provider_id %in% training_provider_ids)

test_data <- model_data_raw |>
  filter(!(provider_id %in% training_provider_ids))

# Confirm that providers do not appear in both datasets.
stopifnot(
  length(intersect(
    unique(training_data$provider_id),
    unique(test_data$provider_id)
  )) == 0,
  nrow(training_data) + nrow(test_data) == nrow(model_data_raw)
)

# Inspect the realised split and outcome distributions.
split_distribution <- bind_rows(
  training_data |> mutate(split = "Training"),
  test_data |> mutate(split = "Test")
) |>
  count(split, rating_tier, name = "n_services") |>
  group_by(split) |>
  mutate(
    percentage = round(100 * n_services / sum(n_services), 1)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

print(split_distribution)



# Provider-grouped five-fold cross-validation



cv_seed <- 5004L
n_folds <- 5L

provider_cv_frame <- provider_split_frame |>
  filter(provider_id %in% training_provider_ids)

set.seed(cv_seed)

provider_validation_folds <- createFolds(
  provider_cv_frame$provider_stratum,
  k = n_folds,
  returnTrain = FALSE
)

# Convert provider-level folds into service-row indices.
cv_index_out <- lapply(
  provider_validation_folds,
  function(provider_rows) {
    validation_provider_ids <- provider_cv_frame$provider_id[provider_rows]

    which(training_data$provider_id %in% validation_provider_ids)
  }
)

# caret requires the complementary training indices.
all_training_rows <- seq_len(nrow(training_data))

cv_index <- lapply(
  cv_index_out,
  function(validation_rows) {
    setdiff(all_training_rows, validation_rows)
  }
)

names(cv_index) <- paste0("Fold", seq_len(n_folds))
names(cv_index_out) <- names(cv_index)

# Confirm that each service appears in exactly one validation fold
# and that no provider crosses training and validation within a fold.
stopifnot(
  all(
    tabulate(
      unlist(cv_index_out),
      nbins = nrow(training_data)
    ) == 1L
  )
)

for (fold_name in names(cv_index)) {
  analysis_providers <- unique(
    training_data$provider_id[cv_index[[fold_name]]]
  )

  validation_providers <- unique(
    training_data$provider_id[cv_index_out[[fold_name]]]
  )

  stopifnot(
    length(intersect(
      analysis_providers,
      validation_providers
    )) == 0
  )
}

cv_fold_summary <- bind_rows(
  lapply(
    names(cv_index_out),
    function(fold_name) {
      training_data[cv_index_out[[fold_name]], ] |>
        count(rating_tier, name = "n_services") |>
        mutate(fold = fold_name)
    }
  )
) |>
  group_by(fold) |>
  mutate(
    percentage = round(100 * n_services / sum(n_services), 1)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(fold, rating_tier, n_services, percentage)

print(cv_fold_summary)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Common outcome and predictor set
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

variable_dictionary <- read_csv(
  "data/processed/acecqa_variable_dictionary.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

predictor_names <- variable_dictionary |>
  filter(role == "Predictor") |>
  pull(variable)

missing_predictors <- setdiff(
  predictor_names,
  names(model_data_raw)
)

if (length(missing_predictors) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Predictor columns are missing: ",
    paste(missing_predictors, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

training_model_data <- training_data |>
  select(
    rating_tier,
    all_of(predictor_names)
  )

test_model_data <- test_data |>
  select(
    rating_tier,
    all_of(predictor_names)
  )

# Confirm that identifiers and rating-derived variables are excluded.
forbidden_predictors <- c(
  "service_id",
  "provider_id",
  "overall_rating_original"
)

stopifnot(
  !any(forbidden_predictors %in% names(training_model_data)),
  identical(
    names(training_model_data),
    names(test_model_data)
  ),
  ncol(training_model_data) == length(predictor_names) + 1L
)

cat(
  "\nOutcome: rating_tier",
  "\nNumber of predictors:", length(predictor_names),
  "\nTraining observations:", nrow(training_model_data),
  "\nTest observations:", nrow(test_model_data),
  "\n"
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fold-wise preprocessing specifications
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

logical_predictors <- variable_dictionary |>
  filter(
    role == "Predictor",
    type == "Logical"
  ) |>
  pull(variable)

# Convert logical predictors using fixed, predefined levels.
training_model_data <- training_model_data |>
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(logical_predictors),
      ~ factor(
        .x,
        levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
        labels = c("No", "Yes")
      )
    )
  )

test_model_data <- test_model_data |>
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(logical_predictors),
      ~ factor(
        .x,
        levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
        labels = c("No", "Yes")
      )
    )
  )

# Operations shared by all five models.
base_recipe <- recipe(
  rating_tier ~ .,
  data = training_model_data
) |>
  step_string2factor(
    all_nominal_predictors()
  ) |>
  step_unknown(
    all_nominal_predictors(),
    new_level = "Unknown"
  ) |>
  step_novel(
    all_nominal_predictors(),
    new_level = "Novel"
  ) |>
  step_other(
    all_nominal_predictors(),
    threshold = 0.01,
    other = "Other"
  ) |>
  step_impute_median(
    all_numeric_predictors()
  ) |>
  step_log(
    provider_service_count,
    offset = 1
  )

# For multinomial logistic regression, LDA, kNN and SVM.
scaled_recipe <- base_recipe |>
  step_normalize(
    all_numeric_predictors()
  ) |>
  step_dummy(
    all_nominal_predictors()
  ) |>
  step_nzv(
    all_predictors()
  )

# For Random Forest, where scaling is unnecessary.
tree_recipe <- base_recipe |>
  step_dummy(
    all_nominal_predictors()
  ) |>
  step_nzv(
    all_predictors()
  )

print(scaled_recipe)
print(tree_recipe)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared evaluation function and caret resampling control
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

macro_f1_summary <- function(data, lev = NULL, model = NULL) {
  if (is.null(lev)) {
    lev <- levels(data$obs)
  }

  f1_by_class <- vapply(
    lev,
    function(class_name) {
      true_positive <- sum(
        data$pred == class_name &
          data$obs == class_name
      )

      false_positive <- sum(
        data$pred == class_name &
          data$obs != class_name
      )

      false_negative <- sum(
        data$pred != class_name &
          data$obs == class_name
      )

      precision_denominator <- true_positive + false_positive
      recall_denominator <- true_positive + false_negative

      precision <- if (precision_denominator == 0) {
        0
      } else {
        true_positive / precision_denominator
      }

      recall <- if (recall_denominator == 0) {
        0
      } else {
        true_positive / recall_denominator
      }

      if (precision + recall == 0) {
        0
      } else {
        2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
      }
    },
    numeric(1)
  )

  recall_by_class <- vapply(
    lev,
    function(class_name) {
      denominator <- sum(data$obs == class_name)

      if (denominator == 0) {
        0
      } else {
        sum(
          data$pred == class_name &
            data$obs == class_name
        ) / denominator
      }
    },
    numeric(1)
  )

  names(recall_by_class) <- paste0(
    "Recall_",
    make.names(lev)
  )

  c(
    Macro_F1 = mean(f1_by_class),
    Accuracy = mean(data$pred == data$obs),
    recall_by_class
  )
}

model_control <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = n_folds,
  index = cv_index,
  indexOut = cv_index_out,
  classProbs = FALSE,
  summaryFunction = macro_f1_summary,
  savePredictions = "final",
  returnResamp = "final",
  allowParallel = TRUE
)

# Check the evaluation function using a majority-class baseline.
majority_class <- names(
  which.max(
    table(training_model_data$rating_tier)
  )
)

baseline_check <- data.frame(
  obs = training_model_data$rating_tier,
  pred = factor(
    rep(
      majority_class,
      nrow(training_model_data)
    ),
    levels = levels(training_model_data$rating_tier)
  )
)

baseline_metrics <- macro_f1_summary(
  baseline_check,
  lev = levels(training_model_data$rating_tier)
)

print(baseline_metrics)


fold1_training <- training_model_data[
  cv_index[["Fold1"]],
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

fold1_validation <- training_model_data[
  cv_index_out[["Fold1"]],
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Learn preprocessing parameters from Fold 1 training data only.
scaled_recipe_check <- prep(
  scaled_recipe,
  training = fold1_training
)

tree_recipe_check <- prep(
  tree_recipe,
  training = fold1_training
)

# Apply the learned parameters to Fold 1 validation data.
scaled_validation_check <- bake(
  scaled_recipe_check,
  new_data = fold1_validation
)

tree_validation_check <- bake(
  tree_recipe_check,
  new_data = fold1_validation
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(scaled_validation_check) == nrow(fold1_validation),
  nrow(tree_validation_check) == nrow(fold1_validation),
  !anyNA(scaled_validation_check),
  !anyNA(tree_validation_check)
)

cat(
  "Scaled recipe output:",
  nrow(scaled_validation_check), "rows ×",
  ncol(scaled_validation_check), "columns\n",
  "Tree recipe output:",
  nrow(tree_validation_check), "rows ×",
  ncol(tree_validation_check), "columns\n"
)

Model Fitting & Improvement

Linear Discriminant Analysis

Preprocessing

In addition to the shared scaled_recipe, the recipe used for Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) also further remove linear dependencies among numeric predictors and dropped predictors correlated above a 0.9 threshold.

Models

Two models of LDA were trained, one using the unchanged training set’s class proportion (lda_fit_emp) and one using equal class priors to account for the class imbalance of the dataset (lda_fit_equal).

For both models, we also performed parameter tuning on dimen — the number of discriminant functions produced. This is limited by the number of classes, resulting in only 2 possible tuning values.

Only one LDA model is included in the final model selection. Due to similar Macro F1 score for both models, lda_fit_equal was chosen due to its better Recall score for Below NQS. Additionally, both model performed better with dimen=2.

lda_prior_comparison <- read.csv("../outputs/lda/lda_prior_comparison.csv") |>
  select(priors, dimen, Macro_F1, Macro_F1SD, Accuracy, starts_with("Recall_")) |>
  mutate(across(c(Macro_F1, Macro_F1SD, Accuracy, starts_with("Recall_")), ~ round(.x,4))) |> 
  select(1:8) |>
  arrange(dimen)
knitr::kable(lda_prior_comparison)

Full model implementation

Model implementation was done in a separate R script model_LDA.R for purpose of organization with steps as described above. It depends on the shared workflow in R/06_model_setup.R. The code is displayed without rerunning the full search during report rendering.

  "caret",
  "recipes",
  "ggplot2"
)

missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(
    required_packages,

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(caret)
library(recipes)
library(ggplot2)
select <- dplyr::select

if (!exists("scaled_recipe")) {source("R/06_model_setup.R")}
dir.create("outputs/lda", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)

# Training Model

lda_recipe <- scaled_recipe %>% # Additional pre-processing
  step_lincomb(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_corr(all_numeric_predictors(), threshold = 0.9)

lda_fit_equal <- train(
  lda_recipe,
  data = training_model_data,
  trControl = model_control,
  method = "lda2",
  metric = "Macro_F1",
  tuneGrid = expand.grid(dimen = 1:2), # Only 2 possible values for hyperparam tuning
  prior = rep(1/3, 3) # Equal class priors
)

lda_fit_emp <- train(
  lda_recipe,
  data = training_model_data,
  trControl = model_control,
  method = "lda2",
  metric = "Macro_F1",
  tuneGrid = expand.grid(dimen = 1:2) # Empirical priors (training class proportions)
)

# Performance on data (cross-validation only)
## With vs. Without Class Priors
### Side by side
lda_prior_comparison <- bind_rows(
  lda_fit_emp$results   |> mutate(priors = "Empirical"),
  lda_fit_equal$results |> mutate(priors = "Equal")
)

print(lda_prior_comparison)

### Per-fold comparison
lda_fold_comparison <- bind_rows(
  lda_fit_emp$resample   |> mutate(priors = "Empirical"),
  lda_fit_equal$resample |> mutate(priors = "Equal")
)

lda_fold_comparison %>%
  group_by(priors) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_macro_f1 = mean(Macro_F1),
    sd_macro_f1   = sd(Macro_F1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

### Paired difference per fold (equal - emp)
lda_paired_diff <- lda_fold_comparison %>%
  select(Resample, priors, Macro_F1) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = priors, values_from = Macro_F1) %>%
  mutate(diff = `Equal` - `Empirical`)
print(lda_paired_diff)

## Out-of-fold predictions for the chosen dimen
lda_tier_levels <- levels(training_model_data$rating_tier)

lda_oof <- lda_fit_equal$pred
if ("dimen" %in% names(lda_oof)) {
  lda_oof <- lda_oof %>% filter(dimen == lda_fit_equal$bestTune$dimen)
}
stopifnot(nrow(lda_oof) == nrow(training_model_data))   # one prediction per service

lda_oof_df <- data.frame(obs = lda_oof$obs, pred = lda_oof$pred)

lda.train.confusion <- confusionMatrix(data = lda_oof_df$pred, reference = lda_oof_df$obs)
lda.train.confusion

# Evaluations (cross-validation only)

## Overall metrics: CV (fold mean) and CV (pooled out-of-fold)
lda_best_row <- lda_fit_equal$results %>% filter(dimen == lda_fit_equal$bestTune$dimen)

lda_overall <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(split = "CV (mean of folds)",
             t(unlist(lda_best_row[, c("Macro_F1", "Accuracy")]))),
  data.frame(split = "CV (pooled out-of-fold)",

)
print(lda_overall)

## Per-class precision / recall / F1
lda_per_class <- function(cm, split) {
  bc <- as.data.frame(cm$byClass)
  bc$class <- sub("^Class: ", "", rownames(bc))
  bc$split <- split
  bc[, c("split", "class", "Precision", "Recall", "F1")]
}

lda_class_metrics <- lda_per_class(lda.train.confusion, "CV (out-of-fold)")
print(lda_class_metrics)

## Baseline vs LDA (majority class per fold, scored on the same validation folds)
fold_baseline <- function(fold) {
  majority <- names(which.max(table(training_model_data$rating_tier[cv_index[[fold]]])))
  rows <- cv_index_out[[fold]]
  d <- data.frame(
    obs  = training_model_data$rating_tier[rows],
    pred = factor(rep(majority, length(rows)), levels = lda_tier_levels)
  )
  as.data.frame(t(macro_f1_summary(d, lev = lda_tier_levels)))
}

lda_vs_baseline <- bind_rows(
  `Majority baseline`  = colMeans(bind_rows(lapply(names(cv_index_out), fold_baseline))),
  `LDA (empirical)`    = unlist(lda_fit_emp$results[lda_fit_emp$results$dimen == lda_fit_emp$bestTune$dimen, ]),
  `LDA (equal priors)` = unlist(lda_fit_equal$results[lda_fit_equal$results$dimen == lda_fit_equal$bestTune$dimen, ]),
  .id = "model"
) |>
  dplyr::select(model, Macro_F1, Accuracy, starts_with("Recall_")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-model, names_to = "metric") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model)

print(lda_vs_baseline)

## Plots
lda_plot_cm <- function(cm, title) {
  df <- as.data.frame(cm$table) %>%
    group_by(Reference) %>%
    mutate(row_pct = 100 * Freq / sum(Freq)) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  ggplot(df, aes(Prediction, Reference, fill = row_pct)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(Freq, "\n(", round(row_pct, 1), "%)")), size = 4) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue", name = "% of true class") +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(levels(df$Reference))) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Predicted rating", y = "Actual rating") +
    coord_fixed() +
    theme_minimal()
}

kNN

Model rationale and fitting

K-nearest neighbours (KNN) was included to assess whether services with similar administrative and provider profiles tend to share an NQS rating tier. The overlap between individual numerical predictors observed in EDA motivates considering their combined local structure. KNN assigns a class using nearby training observations, allowing nonlinear decision boundaries without specifying a parametric form (Schliep & Hechenbichler, 2025). Below NQS, Meeting NQS and Above NQS were treated as nominal classes; their ordering was not explicitly modelled.

The common provider-grouped split contained 13,497 training services and 3,663 held-out services. KNN used the same five provider-grouped training folds as the other candidate models, keeping services from each provider together. This reduces leakage from shared provider characteristics and evaluates transfer to providers absent from the corresponding training partition. Identifiers and rating-derived fields were excluded.

The shared recipes preprocessing pipeline (Kuhn et al., 2026) handled missing and novel categorical levels, pooled levels below 1%, median-imputed numerical predictors, and log(1+x)-transformed provider service count. Numerical predictors were standardised before categorical dummy encoding, followed by near-zero-variance filtering. Scaling prevents variables measured in larger units from dominating Euclidean distances. Dummy columns were not subsequently standardised. Crucially, preprocessing parameters were estimated separately within each fold’s training partition and then applied to validation data. The kknn engine’s additional scaling was disabled (Schliep & Hechenbichler, 2025).

Hyperparameter tuning and improvement

We compared ten neighbour counts, k = 3, 5, 9, 15, 25, 41, 61, 81, 121 and 161, using rectangular (equal) and triangular (distance-weighted) voting: 20 configurations across five folds. Small k permits more local variation, whereas larger k smooths the decision boundary and can favour the dominant class. Triangular voting was tested to give closer neighbours greater influence; it is not class weighting. No class rebalancing was applied. The code expands the search if the overall optimum reaches the largest k; this was unnecessary for the observed optimum.

Selection maximised the unweighted mean fold Macro-F1, the arithmetic mean of the three class F1 scores within each fold. This gives each tier equal evaluation weight despite Meeting NQS comprising 73.7% of training services. Exact ties were resolved by larger k, then alphabetical kernel order.

KNN tuning: best configuration for each kernel on the five shared provider-grouped folds.
Voting kernel Best k Mean Macro-F1 Fold SD Mean accuracy
rectangular 5 0.425 0.025 0.722
triangular 5 0.417 0.012 0.690

The selected configuration was k = 5, equal voting, Euclidean distance. Its mean Macro-F1 was 0.425 (fold SD 0.025), compared with 0.417 for the best triangular configuration, also at k = 5. The difference of 0.008 is descriptive and does not establish statistical superiority. Triangular voting increased mean fold Below NQS recall from 0.044 to 0.067 but reduced Meeting NQS recall from 0.896 to 0.850; the pre-specified Macro-F1 rule therefore retained equal voting.

KNN tuning on the shared training folds. Error bars represent one fold standard deviation, not confidence intervals.

Validation results and interpretation

The majority-class baseline achieved mean fold Macro-F1 0.283 and accuracy 0.737. KNN improved Macro-F1 by 0.142, while accuracy fell to 0.722. This trade-off occurs because Macro-F1 weights classes equally, whereas accuracy is dominated by the number of Meeting NQS observations.

Selected KNN: class metrics from pooled out-of-fold predictions, not held-out test predictions.
Actual tier Support Precision Recall F1
Below NQS 1016 0.206 0.044 0.073
Meeting NQS 9954 0.771 0.897 0.829
Above NQS 2527 0.461 0.310 0.371

Only 45 of 1,016 Below NQS services were correctly identified (recall 0.044); 923 were classified as Meeting NQS. For Above NQS, 784 of 2,527 were identified (recall 0.310), while 1,725 were classified as Meeting NQS. Meeting NQS recall was 0.897. Thus, local profile similarity provides some classification signal but does not reliably distinguish the minority tiers. In particular, the very low Below NQS recall limits usefulness for identifying services that may require additional support or regulatory attention.

The class table pools out-of-fold predictions, giving pooled Macro-F1 0.424; this differs slightly from mean fold Macro-F1 0.425 because fold sizes and distributions differ. The same folds were used for tuning and performance reporting, so these are internal estimates subject to selection optimism. KNN was not evaluated on the held-out test set. In the repository’s common comparison, MLR achieved mean CV Macro-F1 0.4871 and was selected before test scoring; KNN was therefore not the final model.

Limitations and reproducibility

Euclidean distances remain sensitive to redundant predictors and reference-level dummy coding. Median imputation may also obscure structural missingness, and this nominal classifier does not use the tiers’ ordering. Future work could compare reduced feature groups or mixed-data distances within training resampling, with particular attention to Below NQS recall. The administrative snapshot supports association-based classification, not causal claims or validated forecasts of future ratings.

All displayed results are loaded from the supplied repository outputs. To regenerate tuning results and figures, run the following from the repository root; the report itself reads saved results to avoid repeating the full search during knitting.

source("R/07_knn_install.R")
source("R/07_knn.R")

Full KNN implementation

The complete KNN script is displayed below. It includes fold-wise preprocessing, hyperparameter tuning, out-of-fold evaluation, leakage checks and output generation. It depends on the shared workflow in R/06_model_setup.R. The code is displayed without rerunning the full search during report rendering. To regenerate the results, run source("R/07_knn.R") from the repository root.

stopifnot(length(intersect(training_data$provider_id, test_data$provider_id)) == 0L,
          identical(training_model_data$rating_tier, training_data$rating_tier),
          !any(grepl("(^|_)(rating|quality|qa[1-7])(_|$)|^service_id$|^provider_id$",
                     predictor_names, ignore.case = TRUE)),
          length(cv_index) == 5L, identical(names(cv_index), names(cv_index_out)))
audit_rows <- list()
for (f in names(cv_index)) {
  a <- cv_index[[f]]; v <- cv_index_out[[f]]
  stopifnot(length(intersect(a, v)) == 0L,
            setequal(c(a, v), seq_len(nrow(training_model_data))),

            all(table(training_model_data$rating_tier[a]) > 0),

    provider_overlap = 0L, all_classes_present = TRUE)
}
readr::write_csv(dplyr::bind_rows(audit_rows), file.path(out, "leakage_audit.csv"))

# Preprocess separately inside each shared training fold. kknn's internal
# scaling is disabled because the shared recipe already scales numerics.
fold_data <- lapply(names(cv_index), function(f) {
  rec <- recipes::prep(scaled_recipe, training = training_model_data[cv_index[[f]], ])
  list(train = recipes::bake(rec, new_data = training_model_data[cv_index[[f]], ]),
       valid = recipes::bake(rec, new_data = training_model_data[cv_index_out[[f]], ]))
})
names(fold_data) <- names(cv_index)
stopifnot(all(vapply(fold_data, function(x) !anyNA(x$train) && !anyNA(x$valid), logical(1))))
stopifnot(all(vapply(fold_data, function(x) {
  identical(names(x$train), names(x$valid)) &&
    all(vapply(x$train[setdiff(names(x$train), "rating_tier")], is.numeric, logical(1)))
}, logical(1))))

grid <- expand.grid(k = c(3L, 5L, 9L, 15L, 25L, 41L, 61L, 81L, 121L, 161L),
                    kernel = c("rectangular", "triangular"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
results <- list()
predictions <- list()
evaluate_grid <- function(candidates) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(candidates))) {
    k <- candidates$k[i]; kernel <- candidates$kernel[i]
    for (f in names(fold_data)) {
      message("k=", k, ", kernel=", kernel, ", ", f)
      x <- fold_data[[f]]
      fit <- kknn::kknn(rating_tier ~ ., train = as.data.frame(x$train),
                        test = as.data.frame(x$valid), k = k, distance = 2,
                        kernel = kernel, scale = FALSE)
      pred <- factor(fit$fitted.values, levels = levels(training_model_data$rating_tier))
      obs <- x$valid$rating_tier
      metrics <- macro_f1_summary(data.frame(obs = obs, pred = pred))
      results[[length(results) + 1L]] <<- data.frame(k = k, kernel = kernel, fold = f,
                                                   as.list(metrics), check.names = FALSE)
      predictions[[length(predictions) + 1L]] <<- data.frame(k = k, kernel = kernel,
        fold = f, rowIndex = cv_index_out[[f]], obs = obs, pred = pred)
    }
  }
}
summarise_grid <- function() {
  dplyr::bind_rows(results) |>
    dplyr::group_by(k, kernel) |>
    dplyr::summarise(Macro_F1SD = sd(Macro_F1), Macro_F1 = mean(Macro_F1),
                     AccuracySD = sd(Accuracy), Accuracy = mean(Accuracy), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Macro_F1), dplyr::desc(k), kernel)
}
evaluate_grid(grid)
summary <- summarise_grid()
# Expand an upper-bound optimum while keeping k valid for every fold.
max_k <- min(vapply(fold_data, function(x) nrow(x$train) - 2L, integer(1)))
while (summary$k[1] == max(grid$k) && max(grid$k) < max_k) {
  next_k <- min(2L * max(grid$k) + 1L, max_k)
  extra <- expand.grid(k = next_k, kernel = c("rectangular", "triangular"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  evaluate_grid(extra)
  grid <- rbind(grid, extra)
  summary <- summarise_grid()
}
best <- summary[1, ]
fold_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(results)
stopifnot(!anyNA(summary), all(table(fold_results$k, fold_results$kernel) == n_folds))
# Compare the best configuration within each kernel using mean fold metrics.
# Recall is averaged across folds, not calculated from pooled predictions.
kernel_winners <- summary |>
  dplyr::group_by(kernel) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 1L) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
mean_recalls <- fold_results |>
  dplyr::group_by(k, kernel) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::starts_with("Recall_"), mean), .groups = "drop")
kernel_comparison <- dplyr::left_join(kernel_winners, mean_recalls, by = c("k", "kernel"))
readr::write_csv(kernel_comparison, file.path(out, "kernel_comparison.csv"))
all_predictions <- dplyr::bind_rows(predictions)
oof <- all_predictions[all_predictions$k == best$k & all_predictions$kernel == best$kernel, ]
oof <- oof[order(oof$rowIndex), ]
stopifnot(identical(oof$rowIndex, seq_len(nrow(training_model_data))))
oof$service_id <- training_data$service_id[oof$rowIndex]
oof$provider_id <- training_data$provider_id[oof$rowIndex]

class_metrics <- function(obs, pred) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(obs), function(cl) {
    tp <- sum(obs == cl & pred == cl); fp <- sum(obs != cl & pred == cl)
    fn <- sum(obs == cl & pred != cl)
    data.frame(class = cl, support = sum(obs == cl),
      Precision = if (tp + fp == 0) 0 else tp / (tp + fp),
      Recall = if (tp + fn == 0) 0 else tp / (tp + fn),
      F1 = if (2 * tp + fp + fn == 0) 0 else 2 * tp / (2 * tp + fp + fn))
  }))
}
classes <- class_metrics(oof$obs, oof$pred)
cm <- table(Actual = oof$obs, Predicted = oof$pred)
baseline <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(cv_index), function(f) {
  majority <- names(which.max(table(training_model_data$rating_tier[cv_index[[f]]])))
  obs <- training_model_data$rating_tier[cv_index_out[[f]]]
  pred <- factor(rep(majority, length(obs)), levels = levels(obs))
  data.frame(fold = f, as.list(macro_f1_summary(data.frame(obs = obs, pred = pred))))
}))

MLR

Model fitting and rationale

Multinomial logistic regression (MLR) was fitted as an interpretable linear model for the three rating tiers. We used ridge-regularised multinomial regression (glmnet, alpha = 0; Friedman et al., 2010) to stabilise estimation in the presence of related service and provider characteristics. MLR used the 19-predictor recipe described in Preprocessing Recipes, including within-fold median imputation, missing/novel-category handling, dummy encoding, zero-variance removal and normalisation. Unlike the kNN/SVM recipe, it did not log-transform provider_service_count. The service and provider identifiers and rating-derived fields were excluded from model inputs.

To avoid information leakage, preprocessing was estimated separately within each training fold. As described above, the other candidate models used the group’s provider-grouped 80/20 train/test split and five shared provider-grouped cross-validation (CV) folds on the training set. The MLR tuning reported in this section was first run on its own provider-grouped split, which differed from the group’s shared split. The MLR was therefore rerun on the shared split before model selection (see Selected model and test evaluation). The held-out test partition was not used to tune the MLR.

MLR refinement and tuning

Because Meeting NQS accounted for 74.3% of the services, an unweighted model could achieve high accuracy while overlooking smaller classes. We therefore assessed six ridge penalty values (\(\lambda \in \{0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3\}\)) and three weighting schemes (no weights, square-root inverse-frequency weights and capped inverse-frequency weights): 18 configurations in total. Each was evaluated on the same five provider-grouped folds, with mean macro-F1 as the primary selection metric. The macro-F1 calculation included all three classes, assigning an F1 of zero to any class never predicted by a candidate.

On the original MLR split, the selected configuration used \(\lambda = 0.003\) and square-root inverse-frequency class weights. It achieved a mean CV macro-F1 of 0.4859 (SD 0.0151) and mean CV accuracy of 72.92%. The unweighted baseline MLR achieved macro-F1 0.4003 and accuracy 75.47%. Thus, tuning improved macro-F1 by 0.0856 (approximately 21.4% relative) at the cost of 2.55 percentage points of accuracy. This trade-off is consistent with placing more emphasis on minority rating tiers.

Rerunning the same grid on the shared split selected \(\lambda = 0.001\) with the same square-root inverse-frequency weights. This corrected model had a mean CV macro-F1 of 0.4871 (SD 0.0180) and mean CV accuracy of 72.55%. It is the MLR used in the model comparison and test evaluation below; the tables in this section describe the original-split run.

# Five-fold provider-grouped CV results; all three NQS classes included in macro-F1.
mlr_cv_summary <- data.frame(
  Model = c('Unweighted baseline MLR', 'Tuned ridge MLR'),
  `Mean macro-F1` = c(0.4003, 0.4859),
  `Mean accuracy` = c(0.7547, 0.7292),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(mlr_cv_summary, digits = 4,
             caption = 'MLR performance on provider-grouped cross-validation (not the held-out test set).')
MLR performance on provider-grouped cross-validation (not the held-out test set).
Model Mean macro-F1 Mean accuracy
Unweighted baseline MLR 0.4003 0.7547
Tuned ridge MLR 0.4859 0.7292

Class-specific performance

Despite the improvement in macro-F1, the tuned model performed unevenly across the three classes. Mean CV recall was 10.2% for Below NQS, 84.9% for Meeting NQS and 49.3% for Above NQS; mean class-wise F1 was approximately 0.144, 0.827 and 0.487, respectively. The model therefore missed most Below NQS services. Its useful overall discrimination should not be interpreted as reliable identification of potentially underperforming services.

mlr_by_class <- data.frame(
  `Rating tier` = c('Below NQS', 'Meeting NQS', 'Above NQS'),
  `Mean recall` = c(0.102, 0.849, 0.493),
  `Mean F1` = c(0.144, 0.827, 0.487),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(mlr_by_class, digits = 3,
             caption = 'Class-specific mean CV metrics for the selected MLR.')

MLR full implementation

The MLR model was trained, tuned, and evaluated using the following three scripts:

# Run from repository root:
# Rscript run_mlr_baseline.R [path/to/acecqa_analysis.csv] [path/to/output_dir]
# Does not evaluate on test data: the shared holdout must remain untouched
# until group-wide model selection is complete.

required_packages <- c("readr", "rsample", "recipes", "parsnip",
                       "workflows", "tune", "yardstick", "glmnet")
missing_packages <- required_packages[!vapply(required_packages,
                                              requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_packages)) {
  stop("Install packages first: install.packages(c(",
       paste(sprintf('"%s"', missing_packages), collapse = ", "), "))")
}

source("shared/split.R")
source("mlr/preprocessing.R")
source("mlr/model.R")
source("mlr/evaluation.R")

args <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
data_path <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[[1]] else "data/processed/acecqa_analysis.csv"
out_dir <- if (length(args) >= 2) args[[2]] else "outputs/mlr"
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

df <- as.data.frame(readr::read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(df$service_id))
split <- make_group_split(df, test_prop = 0.2, seed = 5003L)
save_split_manifest(df, split, file.path(out_dir, "split_manifest.csv"))
train_raw <- df[split$train, , drop = FALSE]
train <- mlr_model_data(train_raw)
folds <- make_group_folds(train_raw, v = 5L, seed = 5003L)
# Important: the resample object needs the SAME columns as the workflow.
# Rebuild each grouped split with the preselected model data.
folds_model <- lapply(folds$splits, function(s) {
  rsample::make_splits(list(analysis = s$in_id,
                            assessment = setdiff(seq_len(nrow(train)), s$in_id)), train)
})
cv <- rsample::manual_rset(folds_model, ids = folds$id)

# Audit folds, so teammates can reproduce identical provider group assignments.
fold_assign <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(train_raw))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(cv))) {
  assessment_rows <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(train_raw)), cv$splits[[i]]$in_id)
  fold_assign[assessment_rows] <- cv$id[[i]]
}
stopifnot(!anyNA(fold_assign))
utils::write.csv(data.frame(service_id = train_raw$service_id,
                            provider_id = train_raw$provider_id,
                            fold = fold_assign),
                 file.path(out_dir, "cv_fold_manifest.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

wf <- make_mlr_workflow(train, penalty = 0.01)
set.seed(5003L)
res <- tune::fit_resamples(
  wf, resamples = cv,
  metrics = yardstick::metric_set(yardstick::accuracy, yardstick::f_meas),
  control = tune::control_resamples(save_pred = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)
)
pred <- tune::collect_predictions(res)
if (!nrow(pred)) stop("No CV predictions produced; inspect notes:",
                      paste(capture.output(tune::collect_notes(res)), collapse = "\n"))
cv_metrics <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(pred, pred$id), function(p) {
  m <- score_mlr_predictions(p)
  m$fold <- unique(p$id)
  m
}))
utils::write.csv(cv_metrics, file.path(out_dir, "mlr_baseline_cv_metrics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(pred, file.path(out_dir, "mlr_baseline_cv_predictions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
print(aggregate(estimate ~ metric, cv_metrics, mean))

which further calls the scripts:

# Shared provider-aware split utilities (base R only).
# Inputs: data.frame with service_id, provider_id, rating_tier.
# Returns row indices; no provider can appear in more than one partition.

make_group_split <- function(data, test_prop = 0.20, seed = 5003L,
                             candidates = 400L) {
  stopifnot(all(c("service_id", "provider_id", "rating_tier") %in% names(data)))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(data$provider_id), !anyNA(data$rating_tier))
  stopifnot(test_prop > 0, test_prop < 1)
  groups <- unique(as.character(data$provider_id))
  y <- factor(data$rating_tier)
  target <- as.numeric(table(y)) * test_prop
  total_target <- nrow(data) * test_prop
  group_index <- match(as.character(data$provider_id), groups)
  group_class <- rowsum(model.matrix(~ y - 1), group_index, reorder = TRUE)
  # rowsum output indexed by sequential group numbers, in numeric order
  best_loss <- Inf
  best_test_groups <- NULL
  set.seed(seed)
  for (iteration in seq_len(candidates)) {
    chosen <- sample.int(length(groups), size = max(1, round(length(groups) * test_prop)))
    counts <- colSums(group_class[chosen, , drop = FALSE])
    loss <- sum(((counts - target) / pmax(target, 1))^2) +
      ((sum(counts) - total_target) / total_target)^2
    if (all(counts > 0) && loss < best_loss) {
      best_loss <- loss
      best_test_groups <- groups[chosen]
    }
  }
  if (is.null(best_test_groups)) stop("Unable to create split with all classes in test set")
  test_idx <- which(data$provider_id %in% best_test_groups)
  train_idx <- which(!(data$provider_id %in% best_test_groups))
  stopifnot(length(intersect(data$provider_id[train_idx],
                             data$provider_id[test_idx])) == 0)
  list(train = train_idx, test = test_idx, seed = seed,
       test_fraction = length(test_idx) / nrow(data))
}

make_group_folds <- function(train_data, v = 5L, seed = 5003L) {
  stopifnot(v >= 2, "provider_id" %in% names(train_data))
  groups <- unique(as.character(train_data$provider_id))
  if (length(groups) < v) stop("Not enough providers for requested folds")
  # Assign larger providers first; tie order is seeded. Greedily balance
  # service counts, while keeping entire providers inside a single fold.
  sizes <- as.integer(table(factor(train_data$provider_id, levels = groups)))
  set.seed(seed)
  order_groups <- order(-sizes, runif(length(groups)))
  assignment <- integer(length(groups))
  fold_size <- numeric(v)
  for (g in order_groups) {
    f <- which.min(fold_size)
    assignment[g] <- f
    fold_size[f] <- fold_size[f] + sizes[g]
  }
  fold_of_row <- assignment[match(train_data$provider_id, groups)]
  folds <- lapply(seq_len(v), function(f) {
    assessment <- which(fold_of_row == f)
    analysis <- which(fold_of_row != f)
    stopifnot(length(intersect(train_data$provider_id[analysis],
                               train_data$provider_id[assessment])) == 0)
    rsample::make_splits(list(analysis = analysis, assessment = assessment),
                         train_data)
  })
  rsample::manual_rset(folds, ids = paste0("Fold", seq_len(v)))
}

save_split_manifest <- function(data, split, output_path) {
  manifest <- data.frame(
    service_id = data$service_id, provider_id = data$provider_id,
    rating_tier = data$rating_tier,
    partition = ifelse(seq_len(nrow(data)) %in% split$test, "test", "train")
  )
  dir.create(dirname(output_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(manifest, output_path, row.names = FALSE)
  invisible(manifest)
}
# MLR-only features and leakage-safe preprocessing.
# recipe is prepped separately inside each CV analysis fold by workflows.

mlr_feature_names <- function() {
  c("service_type", "state", "number_approved_places", "service_age_years",
    "provider_age_years", "provider_service_count", "operating_pattern",
    "max_weekly_hours", "long_day_care", "preschool_part_school",
    "preschool_standalone", "oshc_after_school", "oshc_before_school",
    "oshc_vacation_care", "other_service", "service_has_conditions",
    "temporarily_closed", "provider_has_conditions",
    "provider_has_trading_name")
}

mlr_model_data <- function(data) {
  cols <- c("rating_tier", mlr_feature_names())
  missing <- setdiff(cols, names(data))
  if (length(missing)) stop("Missing columns: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
  out <- data[, cols, drop = FALSE]
  out$rating_tier <- factor(out$rating_tier,
                            levels = c("Below NQS", "Meeting NQS", "Above NQS"))
  if (anyNA(out$rating_tier)) stop("Unexpected outcome labels")
  # Cast logical Yes/No flags to factors; retain numeric measures as numeric.
  for (name in names(out)) {
    if (name != "rating_tier" && (is.logical(out[[name]]) || is.character(out[[name]]))) {
      out[[name]] <- factor(out[[name]])
    }
  }
  out
}

make_mlr_recipe <- function(training_data) {
  recipes::recipe(rating_tier ~ ., data = training_data) |>
    recipes::step_impute_median(recipes::all_numeric_predictors()) |>
    recipes::step_unknown(recipes::all_nominal_predictors(), new_level = "missing") |>
    recipes::step_novel(recipes::all_nominal_predictors()) |>
    recipes::step_other(recipes::all_nominal_predictors(), threshold = 0.01) |>
    recipes::step_dummy(recipes::all_nominal_predictors()) |>
    recipes::step_zv(recipes::all_predictors()) |>
    recipes::step_normalize(recipes::all_numeric_predictors())
}
# Ridge-regularised multinomial logistic regression using glmnet.
make_mlr_spec <- function(penalty = 0.01) {
  parsnip::multinom_reg(penalty = penalty, mixture = 0) |>
    parsnip::set_engine("glmnet") |>
    parsnip::set_mode("classification")
}

make_mlr_workflow <- function(training_data, penalty = 0.01) {
  workflows::workflow() |>
    workflows::add_recipe(make_mlr_recipe(training_data)) |>
    workflows::add_model(make_mlr_spec(penalty))
}
# Explicit macro-average scoring to avoid ambiguity from metric defaults.
score_mlr_predictions <- function(predictions) {
  
  levels_nqs <- c(
    "Below NQS",
    "Meeting NQS",
    "Above NQS"
  )
  
  truth <- factor(
    predictions$rating_tier,
    levels = levels_nqs
  )
  
  predicted <- factor(
    predictions$.pred_class,
    levels = levels_nqs
  )
  
  cm <- table(truth, predicted)
  
  tp <- diag(cm)
  actual_count <- rowSums(cm)
  predicted_count <- colSums(cm)
  
  precision <- ifelse(
    predicted_count > 0,
    tp / pmax(predicted_count, 1),
    0
  )
  
  recall <- ifelse(
    actual_count > 0,
    tp / pmax(actual_count, 1),
    0
  )
  
  f1 <- ifelse(
    precision + recall > 0,
    2 * precision * recall /
      pmax(precision + recall, .Machine$double.eps),
    0
  )
  
  data.frame(
    metric = c("macro_f1", "accuracy"),
    estimate = c(
      mean(f1),
      sum(tp) / sum(cm)
    )
  )
}

# MLR tuning on the EXACT shared provider-grouped folds.
# Uses recipe from mlr/preprocessing.R (prepared only on each analysis fold).
# F1 for an unpredicted class is zero; all three classes are always included.

mlr_class_levels <- c("Below NQS", "Meeting NQS", "Above NQS")

mlr_fold_scores <- function(truth, pred) {
  truth <- factor(truth, levels = mlr_class_levels)
  pred <- factor(pred, levels = mlr_class_levels)
  stopifnot(!anyNA(truth), !anyNA(pred), length(truth) > 0L)
  m <- table(truth, pred)
  tp <- diag(m)
  p <- ifelse(colSums(m) > 0, tp / pmax(colSums(m), 1), 0)
  r <- ifelse(rowSums(m) > 0, tp / pmax(rowSums(m), 1), 0)
  f1 <- ifelse(p + r > 0, 2 * p * r / pmax(p + r, .Machine$double.eps), 0)
  list(macro_f1 = mean(f1), accuracy = sum(tp) / sum(m),
       per_class = data.frame(class = mlr_class_levels, precision = p,
                              recall = r, f1 = f1, support = rowSums(m)),
       confusion = m)
}

mlr_training_weights <- function(y, scheme = c("none", "sqrt_inverse", "inverse_capped")) {
  scheme <- match.arg(scheme)
  counts <- table(factor(y, levels = mlr_class_levels))
  if (any(counts == 0)) stop("Each training fold must contain every class")
  if (scheme == "none") return(rep(1, length(y)))
  raw <- as.numeric(mean(counts) / counts)
  names(raw) <- names(counts)
  if (scheme == "sqrt_inverse") raw <- sqrt(raw)
  if (scheme == "inverse_capped") raw <- pmin(raw, 5)
  w <- unname(raw[as.character(y)])
  w / mean(w)
}

mlr_load_manifests <- function(df, manifest_dir) {
  a <- utils::read.csv(file.path(manifest_dir, "split_manifest.csv"),
                       colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE)
  b <- utils::read.csv(file.path(manifest_dir, "cv_fold_manifest.csv"),
                       colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE)
  if (anyDuplicated(df$service_id) || anyDuplicated(a$service_id) ||
      anyDuplicated(b$service_id)) stop("Duplicate service_id in data or manifests")
  if (!setequal(as.character(df$service_id), a$service_id))
    stop("Split manifest does not match the supplied dataset")
  a <- a[match(as.character(df$service_id), a$service_id), ]
  if (!all(a$partition %in% c("train", "test"))) stop("Unknown partition")
  if (!identical(as.character(df$provider_id), a$provider_id))
    stop("Provider IDs differ between data and split manifest")
  if (anyDuplicated(a$provider_id[a$partition == "train"]) == 0L) {
    # This is fine: providers may have one service.
  }
  if (length(intersect(unique(a$provider_id[a$partition == "train"]),
                       unique(a$provider_id[a$partition == "test"]))))
    stop("Provider leakage between train and test")
  tr <- which(a$partition == "train")
  if (!setequal(as.character(df$service_id[tr]), b$service_id))
    stop("CV manifest does not match training rows")
  b <- b[match(as.character(df$service_id[tr]), b$service_id), ]
  if (!identical(as.character(df$provider_id[tr]), b$provider_id))
    stop("Provider IDs differ between data and CV manifest")
  if (anyNA(b$fold) || length(unique(b$fold)) != 5L)
    stop("Expected exactly five nonmissing CV folds")
  if (any(tapply(b$fold, b$provider_id, function(z) length(unique(z))) != 1L))
    stop("Provider appears in multiple CV folds")
  list(train_rows = tr, fold = b$fold, fold_ids = sort(unique(b$fold)))
}

mlr_run_tuning <- function(df, manifest_dir, out_dir,
                           lambda_grid = c(0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3),
                           weight_schemes = c("none", "sqrt_inverse", "inverse_capped")) {
  stopifnot(all(lambda_grid > 0), !anyDuplicated(lambda_grid),
            all(weight_schemes %in% c("none", "sqrt_inverse", "inverse_capped")))
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  manifests <- mlr_load_manifests(df, manifest_dir)
  train <- mlr_model_data(df[manifests$train_rows, , drop = FALSE])
  fold_metrics <- list()
  class_metrics <- list()
  all_predictions <- list()
  k <- 0L
  for (fold_id in manifests$fold_ids) {
    idx_train <- which(manifests$fold != fold_id)
    idx_valid <- which(manifests$fold == fold_id)
    training <- train[idx_train, , drop = FALSE]
    validation <- train[idx_valid, , drop = FALSE]
    # Crucial: estimate preprocessing parameters ONLY from this fold's training rows.
    rec <- recipes::prep(make_mlr_recipe(training), training = training, retain = TRUE)
    x_train <- recipes::bake(rec, new_data = training, recipes::all_predictors())
    x_valid <- recipes::bake(rec, new_data = validation, recipes::all_predictors())
    if (!identical(names(x_train), names(x_valid))) stop("Recipe column mismatch")
    x_train <- as.matrix(x_train); x_valid <- as.matrix(x_valid)
    storage.mode(x_train) <- "double"; storage.mode(x_valid) <- "double"
    y_train <- factor(training$rating_tier, levels = mlr_class_levels)
    for (scheme in weight_schemes) {
      message("CV ", fold_id, " | weights=", scheme)
      w <- mlr_training_weights(y_train, scheme)
      # Fit all lambdas in a single glmnet path. 'grouped' multinomial coefficient
      # penalties are not required: use default ungrouped ridge, alpha=0.
      fit <- glmnet::glmnet(
        x = x_train, y = y_train, family = "multinomial", alpha = 0,
        lambda = sort(lambda_grid, decreasing = TRUE), weights = w,
        standardize = FALSE
      )
      for (lam in lambda_grid) {
        y_hat <- as.character(predict(fit, newx = x_valid, s = lam, type = "class"))
        sc <- mlr_fold_scores(validation$rating_tier, y_hat)
        k <- k + 1L
        fold_metrics[[k]] <- data.frame(fold = fold_id, weights = scheme,
                                        lambda = lam, macro_f1 = sc$macro_f1,
                                        accuracy = sc$accuracy,
                                        n_valid = length(idx_valid))
        class_metrics[[k]] <- cbind(data.frame(fold = fold_id, weights = scheme,
                                               lambda = lam), sc$per_class)
        # Only save full OOF prediction records for each configuration; useful for auditing.
        all_predictions[[k]] <- data.frame(
          fold = fold_id, weights = scheme, lambda = lam,
          service_id = as.character(df$service_id[manifests$train_rows[idx_valid]]),
          rating_tier = as.character(validation$rating_tier), .pred_class = y_hat)
      }
    }
  }
  fm <- do.call(rbind, fold_metrics)
  pc <- do.call(rbind, class_metrics)
  pp <- do.call(rbind, all_predictions)
  key <- interaction(fm$weights, fm$lambda, drop = TRUE)
  summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(fm, key), function(z) {
    data.frame(weights = z$weights[1], lambda = z$lambda[1],
               mean_macro_f1 = mean(z$macro_f1), sd_macro_f1 = stats::sd(z$macro_f1),
               mean_accuracy = mean(z$accuracy), folds = nrow(z))
  }))
  summary <- summary[order(-summary$mean_macro_f1, summary$sd_macro_f1,
                           summary$lambda), , drop = FALSE]
  rownames(summary) <- NULL
  if (any(summary$folds != length(manifests$fold_ids))) stop("Incomplete CV grid")
  best <- summary[1, , drop = FALSE]
  utils::write.csv(fm, file.path(out_dir, "mlr_tuning_fold_metrics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(pc, file.path(out_dir, "mlr_tuning_class_metrics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(pp, file.path(out_dir, "mlr_tuning_oof_predictions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(summary, file.path(out_dir, "mlr_tuning_summary.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(best, file.path(out_dir, "mlr_tuning_best_params.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  message("Best CV config (not test-set performance):")
  print(best)
  message("No test set rows used in fitting or tuning.")
  invisible(list(summary = summary, best = best))
}
# Interpretation and shareable CV result export for the selected ridge multinomial MLR.
# Only training partition used. This module does NOT evaluate held-out test rows.

mlr_fit_selected_train <- function(df, manifest_dir, out_dir) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  manifest <- mlr_load_manifests(df, manifest_dir)
  train <- mlr_model_data(df[manifest$train_rows, , drop = FALSE])
  summary_file <- file.path(manifest_dir, 'mlr_tuning_summary.csv')
  if (!file.exists(summary_file)) stop('Missing tuning summary: ', summary_file)
  ranking <- utils::read.csv(summary_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  must <- c('weights','lambda','mean_macro_f1','sd_macro_f1','mean_accuracy','folds')
  if (!all(must %in% names(ranking))) stop('Unexpected tuning summary columns')
  if (anyNA(ranking[, must])) stop('Incomplete tuning summary')
  ranking <- ranking[order(-ranking$mean_macro_f1, ranking$sd_macro_f1, ranking$lambda), ]
  best <- ranking[1L, , drop = FALSE]
  if (best$folds != 5L) stop('Best configuration must have 5 complete folds')
  if (best$weights %notin% c('none','sqrt_inverse','inverse_capped')) stop('Unknown weight scheme')
  if (!is.finite(best$lambda) || best$lambda <= 0) stop('Invalid lambda')

  # Fit preprocessing on training rows only; no test data touched.
  recipe_fit <- recipes::prep(make_mlr_recipe(train), training = train, retain = TRUE)
  features <- recipes::bake(recipe_fit, new_data = train, recipes::all_predictors())
  x <- as.matrix(features)
  storage.mode(x) <- 'double'
  y <- factor(train$rating_tier, levels = mlr_class_levels)
  w <- mlr_training_weights(y, best$weights)
  fitted <- glmnet::glmnet(x, y, family = 'multinomial', alpha = 0,
                          lambda = best$lambda, weights = w, standardize = FALSE)

  # Coefficients represent log odds relative to the other classes in the
  # multinomial softmax parameterisation; exp(beta) is the multiplicative
  # change in exp(eta_class), not a binary one-vs-reference odds ratio.
  coef_by_class <- stats::coef(fitted, s = best$lambda)
  rows <- lapply(names(coef_by_class), function(class_label) {
    cc <- as.matrix(coef_by_class[[class_label]])
    z <- data.frame(class = class_label, feature = rownames(cc),
                    coefficient = as.numeric(cc[, 1L]), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    z$exp_coefficient <- exp(pmax(pmin(z$coefficient, 700), -700))
    z
  })
  coef_table <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  coef_table <- coef_table[order(coef_table$class, -abs(coef_table$coefficient)), ]
  rownames(coef_table) <- NULL
  utils::write.csv(coef_table, file.path(out_dir, 'mlr_selected_coefficients.csv'), row.names = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(coef_table[coef_table$feature != '(Intercept)', ],
                   file.path(out_dir, 'mlr_selected_feature_coefficients.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

  # Uniform group comparison row: all metrics are CV-only; no holdout estimates.
  model_summary <- data.frame(model = 'MLR (ridge, tuned)',
                              cv_scheme = '5-fold provider-grouped',
                              selection_metric = 'macro_f1',
                              cv_mean_macro_f1 = best$mean_macro_f1,
                              cv_sd_macro_f1 = best$sd_macro_f1,
                              cv_mean_accuracy = best$mean_accuracy,
                              penalty = best$lambda,
                              weighting = best$weights,
                              test_metrics_available = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(model_summary, file.path(out_dir, 'mlr_group_comparison.csv'), row.names = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(best, file.path(out_dir, 'mlr_selected_config.csv'), row.names = FALSE)

  saveRDS(list(model = fitted, recipe = recipe_fit,
               model_feature_columns = colnames(x),
               class_levels = mlr_class_levels,
               selected_config = best,
               note = 'Trained on full training partition only; no held-out test evaluation'),
          file.path(out_dir, 'mlr_selected_train_model.rds'))
  message('Selected train-only MLR exported. No test data evaluated.')
  invisible(list(selected = best, coefficients = coef_table, comparison = model_summary))
}
`%notin%` <- function(x, table) !(x %in% table)

Random Forest

Random Forest combines decision trees to capture nonlinear relationships and interactions among service characteristics. We used ranger (Wright & Ziegler, 2017) with 500 trees and Gini splitting. The shared provider-grouped split contained 13,497 training services and 3,663 test services. Tuning used the same five provider-grouped training folds as the group, keeping services from each provider together. Identifiers and rating-derived predictors were excluded.

Within each training fold, the shared tree recipe handled unknown, novel and rare categorical levels, median-imputed numerical missing values, log-transformed provider service count, dummy-encoded categories and removed near-zero-variance predictors. Numerical scaling was not applied. Preprocessing and class weights were estimated from the training portion of each fold, then applied to its validation portion.

We compared eight combinations of two values each for features per split, minimum node size and class weighting. Balanced weights were inverse to training class frequency, giving smaller classes greater weight. The selected configuration maximised mean validation Macro-F1, which equally weights the F1 scores of the three rating tiers.

rf_grid_table <- data.frame(
  Setting = c("Features per split", "Minimum node size", "Class weights", "Trees"),
  Tested = c("5, 12", "5, 20", "Uniform, balanced", "500 (fixed)"),
  Selected = c(rf_best$mtry, rf_best$min_node_size, rf_best$weighting, rf_best$num_trees)
)
knitr::kable(rf_grid_table, caption = "Random Forest tuning settings.")
Random Forest tuning settings.
Setting Tested Selected
Features per split 5, 12 5
Minimum node size 5, 20 20
Class weights Uniform, balanced balanced
Trees 500 (fixed) 500

The selected model achieved mean Macro-F1 0.482 (fold SD 0.027) and mean accuracy 63.02%. The majority-class baseline, which always predicted Meeting NQS, achieved Macro-F1 0.283 and accuracy 73.72%. Thus, RF improved equal-weighted performance across tiers, at the cost of lower overall accuracy.

rf_class_table <- rf_class[c("class", "support", "precision", "recall", "f1")]
knitr::kable(rf_class_table, digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Actual tier", "Services", "Precision", "Recall", "F1"),
  caption = "Random Forest: pooled out-of-fold class performance.")
Random Forest: pooled out-of-fold class performance.
Actual tier Services Precision Recall F1
Below NQS 1016 0.181 0.290 0.223
Meeting NQS 9954 0.821 0.674 0.740
Above NQS 2527 0.414 0.605 0.492

Only 295 of 1,016 Below NQS services were correctly identified (29.0%), so most below-standard services were missed. Class results pool out-of-fold predictions; the overall scores above average fold metrics. These are cross-validation results, not held-out test results. Using the same folds for tuning and reporting can yield optimistic estimates. The eight-setting grid is also limited, and improvement cannot be attributed to weighting alone because other settings varied. RF was refitted on the training set but was not evaluated on the test set.

The folded code below is the actual RF fitting and tuning script. It is displayed rather than rerun during rendering; the tables read its saved outputs.

# Run from the repository root: source("R/07_random_forest.R")
if (!requireNamespace("ranger", quietly = TRUE)) stop("Install ranger first.")
source("R/06_model_setup.R")
dir.create("outputs/random_forest", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("figures/random_forest", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
out <- "outputs/random_forest"
lev <- levels(training_model_data$rating_tier)
grid <- expand.grid(mtry = c(5L, 12L), min_node_size = c(5L, 20L),
                    weighting = c("uniform", "balanced"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
grid$candidate <- seq_len(nrow(grid))
grid$num_trees <- 500L
write_csv(grid, file.path(out, "tuning_grid.csv"))
weights_for <- function(y, mode) {
  if (mode == "uniform") return(rep(1, length(lev)))
  counts <- table(factor(y, levels = lev))
  stopifnot(all(counts > 0))
  as.numeric(length(y) / (length(lev) * counts))
}
fit_rf <- function(x, config, seed, importance = "none") {
  ranger::ranger(rating_tier ~ ., data = as.data.frame(x),
    num.trees = config$num_trees, mtry = config$mtry,
    min.node.size = config$min_node_size, splitrule = "gini",
    class.weights = weights_for(x$rating_tier, config$weighting),
    importance = importance, seed = seed, num.threads = 2L)
}
scores <- list()
predictions <- list()
baseline <- list()
removed <- list()
for (fold in names(cv_index)) {
  tr <- cv_index[[fold]]
  va <- cv_index_out[[fold]]
  fitted_recipe <- prep(tree_recipe, training = training_model_data[tr, ])
  xtr <- juice(fitted_recipe)
  xva <- bake(fitted_recipe, new_data = training_model_data[va, ])
  stopifnot(!anyNA(xtr), !anyNA(xva), max(grid$mtry) < ncol(xtr))
  removed[[fold]] <- tidy(fitted_recipe, number = length(fitted_recipe$steps)) |>
    mutate(fold = fold)
  majority <- names(which.max(table(xtr$rating_tier)))
  base_pred <- factor(rep(majority, length(va)), levels = lev)
  baseline[[fold]] <- data.frame(fold = fold,
    as.list(macro_f1_summary(data.frame(obs = xva$rating_tier, pred = base_pred), lev)))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(grid))) {
    cat("Fitting", fold, "candidate", i, "of", nrow(grid), "\n")
    fit <- fit_rf(xtr, grid[i, ], 7000L + match(fold, names(cv_index)))
    pred <- factor(predict(fit, data = as.data.frame(xva))$predictions, levels = lev)
    stopifnot(!anyNA(pred))
    key <- paste(fold, i, sep = "_")
    scores[[key]] <- data.frame(candidate = i, fold = fold,
      as.list(macro_f1_summary(data.frame(obs = xva$rating_tier, pred = pred), lev)))
    predictions[[key]] <- data.frame(candidate = i, fold = fold, row = va,
      service_id = training_data$service_id[va],
      provider_id = training_data$provider_id[va], obs = xva$rating_tier, pred = pred)
  }
}
fold_scores <- bind_rows(scores)
summary_scores <- fold_scores |>
  group_by(candidate) |>
  summarise(mean_macro_f1 = mean(Macro_F1), sd_macro_f1 = sd(Macro_F1),
            mean_accuracy = mean(Accuracy), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(grid, by = "candidate") |>
  arrange(desc(mean_macro_f1), sd_macro_f1, candidate)
best <- summary_scores[1, ]
oof <- bind_rows(predictions) |> filter(candidate == best$candidate) |> arrange(row)
stopifnot(nrow(oof) == nrow(training_model_data), !anyDuplicated(oof$row))
cm <- as.data.frame(table(Observed = factor(oof$obs, levels = lev),
                         Predicted = factor(oof$pred, levels = lev)))
class_scores <- bind_rows(lapply(lev, function(label) {
  tp <- sum(oof$obs == label & oof$pred == label)
  actual <- sum(oof$obs == label)
  predicted <- sum(oof$pred == label)
  data.frame(class = label, support = actual,
    precision = if (predicted == 0) 0 else tp / predicted,
    recall = tp / actual, f1 = 2 * tp / (actual + predicted))
}))
write_csv(fold_scores, file.path(out, "cv_fold_metrics.csv"))
write_csv(summary_scores, file.path(out, "cv_summary.csv"))
write_csv(bind_rows(baseline), file.path(out, "baseline_cv.csv"))
write_csv(oof, file.path(out, "selected_oof_predictions.csv"))
write_csv(cm, file.path(out, "confusion_matrix.csv"))
write_csv(class_scores, file.path(out, "per_class_metrics.csv"))
write_csv(bind_rows(removed), file.path(out, "removed_predictors.csv"))
saveRDS(list(training_ids = training_data$service_id, test_ids = test_data$service_id,
             cv_index = cv_index, cv_index_out = cv_index_out),
        file.path(out, "shared_split_manifest.rds"))
cat("Refitting chosen configuration on all training observations.\n")
final_recipe <- prep(tree_recipe, training = training_model_data)
final_model <- fit_rf(juice(final_recipe), best, 7503L, importance = "permutation")
saveRDS(list(model = final_model, recipe = final_recipe, configuration = best,
             outcome_levels = lev, test_evaluated = FALSE,
             shared_setup_md5 = tools::md5sum("R/06_model_setup.R")),
        file.path(out, "random_forest_fit.rds"))
importance <- data.frame(feature = names(final_model$variable.importance),
                         importance = unname(final_model$variable.importance)) |>
  arrange(desc(importance))
write_csv(importance, file.path(out, "permutation_importance.csv"))
p <- ggplot(cm, aes(x = Predicted, y = Observed, fill = Freq)) +
  geom_tile() + geom_text(aes(label = Freq)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#60b6a8") +
  labs(title = "Random forest: pooled out-of-fold predictions", fill = "Count") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
ggsave("figures/random_forest/confusion_matrix.png", p, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
top <- head(importance, 15)
p <- ggplot(top, aes(x = reorder(feature, importance), y = importance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#268477") + coord_flip() + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  labs(title = "Training-set OOB permutation importance", x = NULL,
       y = "Permutation importance (not causal)")
ggsave("figures/random_forest/importance.png", p, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 150)
capture.output(sessionInfo(), file = file.path(out, "session_info.txt"))
print(summary_scores)
print(class_scores)
cat("Finished. No held-out test performance was calculated.\n")

Support Vector Machines

Linear SVM Fitting, Tuning and Improvement

Linear SVM uses a linear decision boundary to separate the three rating tiers (Karatzoglou et al., 2004). It used the scaled recipe and the same five-fold provider-grouped cross-validation described earlier.

The unweighted and weighted Linear SVMs were tested using the same \(C\) grid: {0.0078125, 0.03125, 0.0625, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 2, 8}. All unweighted Linear SVM candidates predicted every service as Meeting NQS. Their Macro-F1 and class-specific recalls were therefore almost identical to the majority-class baseline. Since \(C=8\) did not improve Macro-F1 or minority-class recall compared with \(C=2\), the unweighted Linear SVM search was not extended further. Under the 0.001 tie-break rule, the smallest candidate, \(C=0.0078125\), was retained.

Square-root inverse-frequency class weights were then added to give more importance to errors in the two smaller classes. This prevented the Linear SVM from predicting only the majority class and increased its mean cross-validation Macro-F1 from 0.2829 to 0.4398. Within the same planned grid, the weighted Linear SVM achieved its highest mean cross-validation Macro-F1 at \(C=8\). This candidate was used as the starting point for RBF refinement.

Detailed code as follows.

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Linear Support Vector Machine
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

required_svm_packages <- c(
  "kernlab"
)

missing_svm_packages <- required_svm_packages[
  !vapply(
    required_svm_packages,
    requireNamespace,
    logical(1),
    quietly = TRUE
  )
]

if (length(missing_svm_packages) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Install the following packages before running this script: ",
    paste(missing_svm_packages, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

library(kernlab)

source("R/06_model_setup.R")

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Phase 0: input and resampling checks
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

# this section aims to confirm that the shared workflow created the expected
# outcome,predictor set and five-fold resampling structure. Identifier leakage
# and provider overlap must be absent before model fitting begins.

expected_outcome_levels <- c(
  "Below NQS",
  "Meeting NQS",
  "Above NQS"
)

forbidden_predictors <- c(
  "service_id",
  "provider_id",
  "overall_rating_original"
)

split_provider_overlap <- length(
  intersect(
    unique(training_data$provider_id),
    unique(test_data$provider_id)
  )
)

fold_provider_overlap <- vapply(
  names(cv_index),
  function(fold_name) {
    analysis_providers <- unique(
      training_data$provider_id[cv_index[[fold_name]]]
    )

    validation_providers <- unique(
      training_data$provider_id[cv_index_out[[fold_name]]]
    )

    length(
      intersect(
        analysis_providers,
        validation_providers
      )
    )
  },
  integer(1)
)

stopifnot(
  identical(
    levels(training_model_data$rating_tier),
    expected_outcome_levels
  ),
  !any(forbidden_predictors %in% names(training_model_data)),
  identical(
    names(training_model_data),
    names(test_model_data)
  ),
  length(cv_index) == 5L,
  length(cv_index_out) == 5L,
  identical(names(cv_index), names(cv_index_out)),
  split_provider_overlap == 0L,
  all(fold_provider_overlap == 0L)
)

cat(
  "\nPhase 0 checks passed",
  "\nTraining dimensions:",
  nrow(training_model_data), "rows x",
  ncol(training_model_data), "columns",
  "\nTest dimensions:",
  nrow(test_model_data), "rows x",
  ncol(test_model_data), "columns",
  "\nNumber of predictors:",
  ncol(training_model_data) - 1L,
  "\nNumber of CV folds:",
  length(cv_index),
  "\nTrain-test provider overlap:",
  split_provider_overlap,
  "\nMaximum within-fold provider overlap:",
  max(fold_provider_overlap),
  "\n\nTraining outcome counts:\n"
)

print(
  table(training_model_data$rating_tier)
)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Phase 1: Linear SVM single-parameter pilot
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

# Fit C = 1 first to validate the complete recipe-model-metric pipeline before
# launching a larger tuning grid. Five-fold CV means that this single candidate
# requires five separate model fits.

svm_linear_pilot_grid <- data.frame(
  C = 1
)

set.seed(5005L)

svm_linear_pilot_time <- system.time({
  svm_linear_pilot <- train(
    scaled_recipe,
    data = training_model_data,
    method = "svmLinear",
    trControl = model_control,
    tuneGrid = svm_linear_pilot_grid,
    metric = "Macro_F1",
    maximize = TRUE
  )
})

cat(
  "\nLinear SVM pilot completed.\n",
  "Candidate C:", svm_linear_pilot_grid$C, "\n"
)

print(svm_linear_pilot)
print(svm_linear_pilot_time)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Phase 1: pilot validation
# -------------------------------------------------------------------

# Check that all five resamples completed and that every training observation
# received exactly one out-of-fold prediction. These predictions provide
# internal validation without using the test set.

pilot_metric_names <- c(
  "Macro_F1",
  "Accuracy",
  "Recall_Below.NQS",
  "Recall_Meeting.NQS",
  "Recall_Above.NQS"
)

pilot_predictions <- svm_linear_pilot$pred
pilot_resamples <- svm_linear_pilot$resample

predictions_per_row <- table(
  pilot_predictions$rowIndex
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(pilot_resamples) == 5L,
  all(pilot_metric_names %in% names(pilot_resamples)),
  !anyNA(pilot_resamples[, pilot_metric_names]),
  nrow(pilot_predictions) == nrow(training_model_data),
  setequal(
    pilot_predictions$rowIndex,
    seq_len(nrow(training_model_data))
  ),
  all(predictions_per_row == 1L),
  !anyNA(

      c("pred", "obs", "rowIndex", "Resample", "C")

)

  svm_linear_C_00078125$results[, svm_result_columns],

  svm_linear_unweighted_results$Macro_F1

  svm_linear_unweighted_results[

      unweighted_max_macro_f1 - 0.001,

)

  svm_linear_unweighted_results[
    svm_linear_unweighted_results$C == selected_unweighted_C,

  setequal(
    svm_linear_unweighted_results$C,
    c(0.0078125, 0.03125, 0.0625, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 2, 8)
  ),
  all(svm_linear_unweighted_results$Recall_Below.NQS == 0),
  all(svm_linear_unweighted_results$Recall_Meeting.NQS == 1),
  all(svm_linear_unweighted_results$Recall_Above.NQS == 0)
)

)

  all(svm_class_weights > 0)
)

  n_training = as.integer(training_class_counts),
  class_weight = as.numeric(svm_class_weights),
  row.names = NULL
)

svm_linear_weighted_C_00625_time <- system.time({

    scaled_recipe,
    data = training_model_data,
    method = "svmLinear",
    trControl = coarse_control_verbose,
    tuneGrid = data.frame(C = 0.0625),
    metric = "Macro_F1",
    maximize = TRUE,
    class.weights = svm_class_weights
  )
})

cat(

  "\n\nCross-validation results:\n"
)

print(svm_linear_weighted_C_00625$results)

cat("\nElapsed time:\n")
print(svm_linear_weighted_C_00625_time)
